output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Getting started with bottom-UpR}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

`bottom-UpR` separates the *response support* from the *likelihood*. COUNT
responses are candidates for Poisson and negative binomial models. PPB
responses are candidates for Gamma and lognormal models.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit <- bottom_up(
  data = ea,
  response = "population",
  buildings = "buildings",
  covariates = c("x1","x2"),
  coords = c("x","y")
)
print(fit)
```

For count responses, mapped buildings enter as a log exposure. For PPB
responses, building exposure is not part of the likelihood; population is
obtained from PPB multiplied by mapped buildings. Exposure is therefore used
exactly once.
